components.name: andromeda-button

components.description: A sci-fi / blueprint-aesthetic button with five variants (default, outline, ghost, destructive, link), three sizes (small, medium, large), optional leading icon, and full hover / focus / active / disabled state coverage. Transparent hairline surfaces sit on a near-black canvas, with an electric-blue accent that brightens and glows on interaction. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: meet-the-crew
components.title: Meet the Crew
components.description: A swipeable portrait card stack perfect for introducing a team, showcasing crew members, or picking an avatar. Four stacked cards fan out with soft rotations: drag to browse, tap to choose. Drop in your own photos and names for an About Us section, a character selector, or an onboarding profile picker. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.description: Five polaroid photo cards stacked in a casual pile. Click to fan them out in a spring-animated arc, hover to lift, click a card to spotlight it. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: product-card-deck
components.title: Product Card Deck
components.description: A draggable card deck you flick through one card at a time. The top card leans toward your drag, then spins away with momentum to reveal the next, and the deck loops endlessly. Every card pairs a picture with a title and a pill action button with hover and press states. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: radial-cards
components.title: Radial Cards
components.description: Seven health-metric cards bloom into a slowly rotating flower. Tap any petal to pull it forward and read your stats up close. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: radial-toolbar
components.title: Radial Toolbar
components.description: A radial context menu that fans out formatting tools around a centre button, with active toggle states and an animated label pill. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: responsive-letters
components.title: Responsive Letters
components.description: Interactive text where each letter responds to cursor proximity, animating variable font properties (weight, stretch, italic, letter-spacing, skew) to create a deformation-under-pressure effect. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: ripple-type
components.title: Ripple Type
components.description: SVG text animation warped by a turbulence filter. Toggle the fan and letters ripple. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: runway-loader
components.title: Runway Loader
components.description: An airplane taxis down a runway progress bar, nose tilting up and taking off at 100%. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: scramble-text
components.title: Scramble Text
components.description: Two words scramble continuously in a pixel cipher. Hover the container to decrypt them one by one. Mouse out and they snap back to noise. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: scroll-wipe-gallery
components.title: Scroll Wipe Gallery
components.description: A full-bleed, scroll-driven photo gallery. Each photo wipes in from a different edge. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: signature-pad
components.title: Signature Pad
components.description: A signature pad widget: pill button morphs into a canvas to draw with mouse or touch. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: slice-type
components.title: Slice Type
components.description: A typographic magic trick. At rest you read one ambiguous word; hover and it splits into two: LIGHT lifting up, NIGHT sinking down, the shared letters resolving into separate glyphs. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: slide-deck
components.title: Slide Deck
components.description: Swipeable card deck with four editorial slides. Navigate forward and back by drag or tap. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: sphere-lines
components.title: Wireframe Globe
components.description: An animated wireframe globe background. A narrow wave band drifts slowly across the surface, and hovering ripples the lines under your cursor. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: stack-tower
components.title: Stack Tower
components.description: A column of 12 stacked words that reads as a rotating 3D cylinder. 2D transforms skew, scale and shift each row so the rotation travels down the stack. Hover lights one row in warm orange without breaking the rhythm. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: sticker-wall
components.title: Sticker Wall
components.description: A draggable sticker card wall. Drop notes, toss emoji, pile them up with real 2D physics. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: taga-toggle
components.title: Taga Toggle
components.description: A playful pill toggle with an expressive face on the thumb: dead (×× eyes, flat mouth) when off, happy (arc eyes, big smile) when on. Track warms from grey to yellow. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: task-cards
components.title: Task Cards
components.description: A swipeable project task card stack where each card has a unique accent colour, status badge, and due date. Drag left or right to cycle through tasks. The dismissed card springs back to the bottom of the deck. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: text-blur-reveal
components.title: Text Blur Reveal
components.description: Words animate into view one by one with a satisfying blur-to-sharp entrance, auto-replaying in a loop. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: tilted-coverflow
components.title: Tilted Coverflow
components.description: 3D coverflow card carousel of seven tilted photos. Drag or arrows to focus any card. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: upload-progress
components.title: Upload Progress
components.description: A collapsible file upload widget with a shimmer progress bar (indigo while uploading, amber on pause). Expand to see per-file rows with live progress, time remaining, and pause, resume, refresh, and stop controls. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: voice-chat-pill
components.title: Live Session Pill
components.description: A compact live-session presence pill with an animated speaking indicator and overlapping avatars. Clicks open a soft-UI modal showing all participants with a Join Now button. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: wave-lines
components.title: Wave Lines
components.description: An animated line background. Dense vertical lines ripple with two layered sine waves, bunching and breathing. Hover to send waves across the canvas. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: wild-morph
components.title: Wild Morph
components.description: Italic SVG word that warps under the cursor, a spring-physics text animation. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: x-grid
components.title: X Grid
components.description: An animated X grid background. Marks illuminate and connect to their neighbors with constellation lines as your cursor passes. Free account required to install; source is free to read.

components.name: color-picker
components.title: Amplo Color Picker
components.description: OKLCH-native, Display-P3-aware color picker built on Base UI primitives — Hue/Lightness/Alpha on Slider, FormatSwitcher on Select, ChannelInput on NumberField, Swatches on RadioGroup. Pulls the shared OKLCH engine and pointer-driven parts (Area, Chroma, GamutBadge, ContrastReadout, Preview, EyeDropper, CssInput) as a registry dependency.

components.name: gradient-picker
components.title: Amplo Gradient Picker
components.description: Linear / radial / conic gradient editing on Base UI primitives — TypeSwitcher/InterpSwitcher/RadialSizeSelect on Select, ReverseStops and the StopList editor as semantic buttons, and a StopEditor composed from this variant's own Hue/Alpha/FormatSwitcher/ChannelInput. Pulls the color picker plus the shared gradient engine (Bar, Area, Overlay, pads, Presets, CssInput, stop popover shell) as registry dependencies.

components.name: fill-picker
components.title: Amplo Fill Picker
components.description: Color + gradient + the solid/gradient mode switcher (FillPicker.Root/Tabs/Tab/Pane) — the "give me everything" entry point, Base UI variant. Pulls the Base UI color and gradient pickers plus the shared fill switcher parts as registry dependencies.

components.name: color-picker-radix
components.title: Amplo Color Picker (Radix)
components.description: Radix/shadcn-classic shells for the Amplo color picker — Hue, Lightness, Alpha, FormatSwitcher, ChannelInput, Swatches, GamutBadge and ContrastReadout built on shadcn's Select and Tooltip. The OKLCH engine, contexts and pointer-driven parts come from the shared color engine, pulled in as a registry dependency.

components.name: gradient-picker-radix
components.title: Amplo Gradient Picker (Radix)
components.description: Radix/shadcn-classic shells for the Amplo gradient picker — TypeSwitcher, InterpSwitcher and RadialSizeSelect on shadcn's Select, plus the popover stop editor. Gradient parsing, contexts and the pointer-driven parts (Bar, Overlay, Area, StopList, angle/position pads, Presets) come from the shared gradient engine, pulled in as a registry dependency.

components.name: fill-picker-radix
components.title: Amplo Fill Picker (Radix)
components.description: Radix/shadcn-classic entry point for the Amplo fill picker — the barrel that composes the Radix color and gradient pickers with the shared solid/gradient mode switcher (FillPicker.Root/Tabs/Tab/Pane), pulled in as registry dependencies.

components.name: color-picker-engine
components.title: Amplo Color Picker Engine
components.description: Dialect-agnostic core of the Amplo color picker: the OKLCH state engine (types, conversions, gamut math, CSS Color 4 chroma reduction, WCAG + APCA contrast), the React context, and the pointer/canvas-driven parts both variants share — Root, Area, Chroma, Preview, EyeDropper, CssInput, Field, and the tooltip-agnostic GamutBadge/ContrastReadout logic. Installed automatically as a dependency of `color-picker` (Base UI) and `color-picker-radix`; you do not normally add it directly.

components.name: gradient-picker-engine
components.title: Amplo Gradient Picker Engine
components.description: Dialect-agnostic core of the Amplo gradient picker: CSS gradient parsing/serialization with per-stop format state, the gradient context and hook, and the pointer-driven parts both variants share — Bar (with its stop-editor slot), Overlay, Area, StopList, StopColor, angle/position pads and inputs, ShapeSwitcher, ReverseStops, RepeatingToggle, Presets, CssInput, and the anchor-only stop popover shell. Installed automatically as a dependency of `gradient-picker` (Base UI) and `gradient-picker-radix`; you do not normally add it directly.

components.name: fill-picker-engine
components.title: Amplo Fill Picker Engine
components.description: Dialect-agnostic core of the Amplo fill picker: the solid/gradient mode state (fill context + `useFillPicker`) and the FillPicker.Root/Tabs/Tab/Pane parts both variants share. Installed automatically as a dependency of `fill-picker` (Base UI) and `fill-picker-radix`; you do not normally add it directly.

components.name: legal1
components.title: Cookie Consent Banner
components.description: Displays a cookie notification with accept, reject, and customize buttons. Perfect for GDPR-compliant websites requiring user consent.

components.name: legal2
components.title: Privacy Policy Accordion
components.description: Shows privacy policy content with expandable accordion sections for each topic. Perfect for organizing lengthy privacy policies into scannable segments.

components.name: legal3
components.title: Terms of Service Summary
components.description: Displays key terms with color-coded icons for allowed, prohibited, and important points. Perfect for presenting condensed terms before user acceptance.

components.name: legal4
components.title: GDPR Data Rights Panel
components.description: Lists user data rights (access, rectify, erase, restrict, export) with request buttons. Perfect for GDPR compliance portals allowing users to exercise their rights.

components.name: legal5
components.title: Data Processing Agreement Card
components.description: Shows DPA details with controller/processor parties, dates, and processing purposes. Perfect for displaying B2B data processing contracts with status badges.

components.name: legal6
components.title: Consent Preferences Manager
components.description: Displays cookie categories with toggle switches to manage consent preferences. Perfect for allowing users to customize their privacy settings granularly.

components.name: legal7
components.title: Legal Disclaimer Banner
components.description: Shows a disclaimer message with warning or info styling and last updated date. Perfect for displaying liability warnings and informational notices.

components.name: legal8
components.title: Age Verification Gate
components.description: Displays an age verification prompt with configurable minimum age and confirm/deny buttons. Perfect for age-restricted content or product pages.

components.name: legal9
components.title: Copyright Footer
components.description: Shows copyright notice, trademark attributions, and links to legal pages. Perfect for website footers requiring comprehensive legal information.

components.name: legal10
components.title: DMCA Takedown Notice
components.description: Guides users through DMCA submission with numbered steps and warnings. Perfect for copyright protection pages accepting infringement reports.

components.name: legal11
components.title: Compliance Checklist
components.description: Displays regulatory requirements with checkmarks, progress bar, and completion percentage. Perfect for showcasing compliance status across multiple standards.

components.name: legal12
components.title: NDA Template Card
components.description: Shows NDA details with type (mutual/unilateral), duration, and key terms covered. Perfect for presenting confidentiality agreement summaries with download options.

components.name: legal13
components.title: Software License Card
components.description: Displays license type with allowed permissions and limitations in checkmark format. Perfect for open-source projects or software documentation pages.

components.name: legal14
components.title: Compliance Badges Grid
components.description: Shows certification badges in a grid with verified checkmarks and in-progress states. Perfect for trust pages displaying security and compliance credentials.

components.name: legal15
components.title: Data Retention Policy
components.description: Lists data categories with types, retention periods, and deletion methods. Perfect for transparency pages explaining how long user data is stored.

components.name: legal16
components.title: Cookie Categories Explainer
components.description: Explains cookie types (essential, functional, analytics, marketing) with icons and examples. Perfect for cookie policy pages educating users on tracking technologies.

components.name: legal17
components.title: Document Version Timeline
components.description: Shows document revision history in a vertical timeline with version numbers and summaries. Perfect for tracking changes to terms, policies, or legal agreements.

components.name: legal18
components.title: Legal Contact Card
components.description: Displays legal department contact information including address, email, phone, and hours. Perfect for providing users a way to reach legal teams with inquiries.

components.name: legal19
components.title: Accessibility Statement
components.description: Shows WCAG conformance level, accessibility features, and issue reporting options. Perfect for demonstrating commitment to digital accessibility standards.

components.name: legal20
components.title: Financial Disclaimer
components.description: Displays investment risk warnings with gain/loss icons and bullet-point cautions. Perfect for fintech or investment platforms requiring regulatory disclosures.

components.name: legal21
components.title: Medical Disclaimer
components.description: Shows healthcare warnings with an emergency notice section for critical situations. Perfect for health-related websites requiring medical advice disclaimers.

components.name: legal22
components.title: Affiliate Disclosure
components.description: Displays FTC-compliant disclosure with affiliate network badges and transparency text. Perfect for content sites monetized through affiliate marketing.

components.name: legal23
components.title: Testimonial Disclaimer
components.description: Shows disclaimer about customer testimonials with star decoration and important notes. Perfect for product pages featuring reviews or success stories.

components.name: legal24
components.title: Earnings Disclaimer
components.description: Displays income disclaimer with warnings about results varying based on effort. Perfect for courses, coaching programs, or business opportunity pages.

components.name: legal25
components.title: Refund Policy Card
components.description: Shows refund period badge, eligible conditions, and exclusions with a request button. Perfect for e-commerce stores displaying return and refund terms.

components.name: legal26
components.title: Data Breach Notification
components.description: Incident notification card for data breaches with severity badge, affected data types, timeline, and recommended actions. Suitable for security incident pages and user notifications.

components.name: legal27

components.description: Transparency card disclosing the use of AI and automated decision-making. Lists AI capabilities, data usage, and opt-out options. Compliant with EU AI Act and emerging regulations.

components.name: legal28

components.name: legal29

components.description: Lists allowed and prohibited usage of a service or platform with check and cross icons. Includes a violation reporting section. Suitable for SaaS, hosting, and community platforms.

components.name: legal30

components.description: Service Level Agreement card showing uptime guarantee percentage, compensation tiers for downtime, and incident response times. Ideal for SaaS and cloud service providers.

components.description: Outlines the dispute resolution process with numbered steps from informal negotiation to binding arbitration. Includes governing law and jurisdiction details.

components.name: legal34

components.name: dotm-square-8

components.name: dotm-square-9

components.name: dotm-square-10

components.name: dotm-square-11

components.description: Concentric diamond ripple with a soft secondary echo pulse per ring.

components.name: dotm-square-12
components.title: Origin Wave

components.name: dotm-square-13
components.title: Core Rotor

components.name: dotm-square-14
components.title: Prism Bloom

components.name: dotm-square-15
components.title: Helix Glow

components.name: dotm-square-16
components.title: Helix Core

components.name: dotm-square-17
components.title: Half Helix
components.description: Single-strand helix variant that shows one side of the DNA wave.

components.name: dotm-square-18
components.title: Sound Bars
components.description: Equalizer-style vertical bars that pulse like live music levels.

components.name: dotm-square-19
components.title: Infinity Run
components.description: Dual counter-rotating heads trace a figure-eight with a soft crossover pulse at center.

components.name: dotm-square-20
components.title: Mobius Run
components.description: A bright head and tail run around the outer ring; a dimmer second train stays half a lap behind, with inner corner flashes for the twist.

components.name: dotm-circular-1
components.title: Halo Drift
components.description: A circular-masked half-helix that travels diagonally from top-left to bottom-right with a bright strand and soft adjacent trail.

components.name: dotm-circular-2
components.title: Tri Orbit
components.description: Three luminous heads orbit the circular ring at equal offsets, creating a triad chase that never overlaps into the old snake rhythm.

components.name: dotm-circular-3
components.title: Plasma Veil
components.description: A plasma-like diagonal sweep and pulsing core weave through the circular mask for a distinctly different motion signature.

components.name: dotm-circular-4
components.title: Radar Arc
components.description: A rotating radar arm scans the circular grid with a bright beam front, soft wake, and faint perimeter ring echo.

components.name: dotm-circular-5
components.title: Nova Wheel
components.description: Four rotating pinwheel blades spin through the circular matrix with a glowing center and soft trailing halo.

components.name: dotm-circular-6
components.title: Phase Orb
components.description: An off-center orbiting energy point traces a phase-shifted loop, creating a drifting orbital glow inside the circular matrix.

components.name: dotm-circular-7
components.title: Gate Shift
components.description: A scanning gate flips between vertical and horizontal sweeps, producing a crisp alternating shutter rhythm in the circular grid.

components.name: dotm-circular-8
components.title: Heart Pulse
components.description: Pulse bursts from the center with a dual-beat cadence, sending soft concentric pressure waves across the circular matrix.

components.name: dotm-circular-9
components.title: Star Compass
components.description: A cardinal beacon pattern: N/E/S/W sectors pulse in sequence with a dim opposite echo, creating a clear directional rhythm in the circular mask.

components.name: dotm-circular-10
components.title: Binary Bloom
components.description: Binary-style opacity tiers pulse in modular steps so only a few cells peak at once while others stay low, producing a crisp coded bloom.

components.name: dotm-circular-11
components.title: Lunar Breathe
components.description: A rotating crescent moon silhouette: bright lunar body, soft rim, and faint directional halo moving around the circular mask.

components.name: dotm-circular-12
components.title: Arc Beacon
components.description: A stepped 8-direction beacon beam sweeps around the circle with a dim opposite echo and diagonal spoke accents.

components.name: dotm-circular-13
components.title: Twin Helix
components.description: A circular-masked twin-helix: mirrored side strands weave inward and outward with intermittent interior bridge pulses.

components.name: dotm-circular-14
components.title: Rung Shift
components.description: A shifting DNA ladder where a bright horizontal rung steps row-by-row while side anchors sway and leave soft ghost echoes.

components.name: dotm-circular-15
components.title: Glyph Cluster
components.description: Braille-inspired grouped dot motifs cycle through rails, bridges, and cross forms inside the circular mask with crisp tiered opacity.

components.name: dotm-circular-16
components.title: Rail Scan
components.description: A braille rail scanline sweeps row-by-row between left and right cells, with near-column accents and soft trail falloff.

components.name: dotm-circular-17
components.title: Checker Shift
components.description: Braille-biased checker phases alternate in stepped shifts, keeping rails pronounced while the center cross supports readability.

components.name: dotm-circular-18
components.title: Pulse Pair
components.description: Mirrored braille dot pairs pulse from top and bottom toward the center, with a connective center-column accent.

components.name: dotm-circular-19
components.title: Orbit Cell
components.description: A bright braille cell head orbits the inner ring with a dim tail while rail columns remain softly active.

components.name: dotm-circular-20
components.title: Glyph Cycle
components.description: Distinct braille-like glyphs cycle in sequence with previous-frame ghosting for a crisp readable symbol transition.

components.name: dotm-triangle-1
components.title: Core Spokes
components.description: A triangle-masked matrix where three spoke lines originate at the center and travel outward to each triangle edge.

components.name: dotm-triangle-2
components.title: Altitude Wave
components.description: A soft altitude wave travels between apex and base while the center column remains gently present for shape readability.

components.name: dotm-triangle-3
components.title: Corner Bounce
components.description: A single head bounces between triangle corners along the perimeter path with a short fading tail.

components.name: dotm-triangle-4
components.title: Vertex Chase
components.description: Three staggered heads chase around the triangle perimeter, leaving short fading tails while all dots stay fixed in place.

components.name: dotm-triangle-5
components.title: Row Sweep
components.description: A reflected scanline sweeps from apex to base and back, animating only opacity bands across triangle rows.

components.name: dotm-triangle-6
components.title: Braille Beat
components.description: Triangle-masked braille dots fill down the left rail, then the right, then blink full and empty.

components.name: dotm-triangle-7
components.title: Oblique Weave
components.description: Diagonal harmonics keyed on row + col: bright bands glide along oblique lines through the triangle with a subtle second harmonic for texture.

components.name: dotm-triangle-8
components.title: Wing Metronome
components.description: The lower triangle splits into left and right wings that trade emphasis on a pendulum beat; apex and center pulse brightest when both sides meet in the middle.

components.name: dotm-triangle-9
components.title: Corona Tier
components.description: Eight-connected distance rings from the heart cell: a bright corona sweeps outward through discrete tiers then back, so depth reads as concentric energy shells.

components.name: dotm-triangle-10
components.title: Column Rake
components.description: A stepped head and tail snake the mask in strict column order (bottom to top per column, columns left to right), unlike perimeter chases or diagonal waves.

components.name: dotm-triangle-11
components.title: Shelf Descent
components.description: Cosine bands keyed on Manhattan distance from the apex (not the center): energy reads as horizontal tiers dropping through the triangle.

components.name: dotm-triangle-12
components.title: Skew Drift
components.description: Traveling harmonics on `row - col` so bright ridges move along NE–SW obliques, orthogonal in feel to diagonal loaders that use `row + col`.

components.name: dotm-triangle-13
components.title: Serpent Zip
components.description: A stepped snake follows row-wise serpentine order (base left→right, then alternating row directions) with a long tail — zigzag motion, not a column path.

components.name: dotm-triangle-14
components.title: Pillar Sweep
components.description: A smooth vertical beam sweeps grid columns 0→6; only triangle-masked dots respond so the silhouette lights one vertical slice at a time.

components.name: dotm-triangle-15
components.title: Tripod Handoff
components.description: Brightness hands off smoothly among the three silhouette vertices (apex, left base, right base) with Manhattan falloff — a corner-to-corner orbit, not a mod-3 lattice.

components.name: dotm-triangle-16
components.title: Updraft
components.description: A V-shaped thermal ridge moves through row-and-column space: brightness peaks along an inverted V so the front climbs the two lower flanks toward the apex, not a flat horizontal row scan like Row Sweep.

components.name: dotm-triangle-17
components.title: Infinity Trace
components.description: A stepped head and tail follow a single 10-cell path: left base up to the apex, down the right rim, then through (4,4) → center → (4,2) for a crossing loop.

components.name: dotm-triangle-18
components.title: Hollow Shell
components.description: The heart cell stays locked dim while every other triangle dot breathes together in phase — a hollow, ring-like pulse.

components.name: dotm-triangle-19
components.title: Pivot Ray
components.description: A Gaussian wedge of brightness rotates around the heart cell using each dot’s polar angle — a clear pivoting searchlight, not a cosine-product moiré field.

components.name: dotm-triangle-20
components.title: Twin Perimeter
components.description: Two stepped heads chase the outer perimeter path half a lap apart, each with its own tail; the heart cell stays quietly dim off the loop.

components.name: dotm-hex-1
components.title: Hex Orbit
components.description: A 3-4-5-4-3 hexagonal dot field with two soft perimeter heads chasing around the shell while the center stays quietly lit.

components.name: dotm-hex-2
components.title: Prism Bloom
components.description: Three rotating spokes sweep through the hex field with a soft outer shell pulse and a breathing center point.

components.name: dotm-hex-3
components.title: Honey Gate
components.description: Two diagonal bands slide through the honeycomb from opposite sides, meeting in a bright center flash before opening again.

components.name: dotm-hex-4
components.title: Vertex Relay
components.description: A bright signal hands off around the hex vertices while inner echo dots answer each corner and the center keeps a quick pulse.

components.name: dotm-hex-5
components.title: Spiral Lattice
components.description: Counter-rotating spiral waves cross through the hex lattice, creating a fast core pulse and softer outer wake.

components.name: dotm-hex-6
components.title: Chevron March
components.description: Smooth chevron bands flow through the hex field in a wrapped loop, keeping an obvious arrow pattern without a reset snap.

components.name: dotm-hex-7
components.title: Hourglass Flip
components.description: Top and bottom bars squeeze into a bright center hourglass, then flip into side rails and a diamond.

components.name: dotm-hex-8
components.title: Glyph Flip
components.description: Crisp symbolic masks flip between stars, chevrons, and rails for a snappy pixel-glyph loader.

components.name: dotm-hex-9
components.title: Petal Shimmer
components.description: A four-petal highlight rotates through the hex with a soft shell sheen and steady center glow.

components.name: dotm-hex-10
components.title: Liquid Vortex
components.description: Refined swirl bands and a slower lens highlight create a smoother liquid shimmer through the hex lattice.

components.description: A compact 3×3 grid with a four-dot tail spiraling clockwise from the outer border toward the center.

components.name: dotm-3x3-2

components.description: Diagonal bands pulse in sequence across the 3×3 grid from the top-right corner toward the bottom-left.

components.name: dotm-3x3-3
components.title: Drift TL
components.description: Diagonal bands pulse in sequence across the 3×3 grid from the top-left corner toward the bottom-right.

components.name: dotm-3x3-4
components.title: Drift BR
components.description: Diagonal bands pulse in sequence across the 3×3 grid from the bottom-right corner toward the top-left.

components.name: dotm-3x3-5
components.title: Drift BL
components.description: Diagonal bands pulse in sequence across the 3×3 grid from the bottom-left corner toward the top-right.

components.name: dotm-3x3-6
components.title: Core Echo
components.description: Manhattan rings ripple outward from the center cell, expanding through the 3×3 grid in even steps.

components.name: dotm-3x3-7
components.title: Column Flux
components.description: Vertical bands pulse in sequence from the left column through the right, lighting all three rows in each column together.

components.name: dotm-3x3-8
components.title: Row Sweep
components.description: Horizontal bands pulse in sequence from the top row down through the bottom of the 3×3 matrix.

components.name: dotm-3x3-9
components.title: Serpent
components.description: A narrow pulse travels the full serpentine path across all nine cells, row by row.

components.name: dotm-3x3-10
components.title: Frame Chase
components.description: A highlight runs clockwise around the outer frame while the center cell holds a steady pulse.

components.name: dotm-3x3-11
components.title: Glyph Pulse
components.description: Bold symbol motifs flash in sequence — corners, cross, full grid, center, ring, X, and side rails — like a tiny pixel display.

components.name: dotm-3x3-12
components.title: Drop Ripple
components.description: Concentric ripples expand from the center of the 3×3 grid, like a stone dropped in still water.

components.name: dotm-3x3-13
components.title: Right Surge
components.description: A vertical wave pulse sweeps from the right column toward the left, illuminating every row in each band together.

components.name: dotm-3x3-14
components.title: Comet Trail
components.description: A bright comet with a two-dot tail races clockwise around the outer frame while the center cell softly breathes.

components.name: dotm-3x3-15
components.title: Echo Rings
components.description: Soft square ripples echo outward from the center through Manhattan rings, with a gentle alternating shimmer.

components.name: dotm-3x3-16
components.title: Smiley Spin
components.description: A pixel smiley face rotates continuously in the 3×3 grid.

components.name: dotm-3x3-18
components.title: Check Spin

components.name: dotm-3x3-19
components.title: Arrow Spin

components.name: dotm-3x3-20
components.title: Corner Spin
components.description: An L-shaped pixel corner rotates continuously in the 3×3 grid.

components.title: Play Spin

components.name: brand-visual-asset-generator
components.title: Brand Visual Asset Generator
components.description: Generate brand-aligned SVG asset packs for SaaS products using Context.dev brand extraction and a Quiver Arrow SVG tool.

overview: Brand Visual Asset Generator is an on-demand eve agent that turns a company domain, product description, or explicit brand profile into a coherent pack of editable SVG assets: icons, empty states, hero illustrations, badges, feature graphics, onboarding visuals, changelog art, and dashboard or modal graphics. You talk to it in your eve chat client, name the assets you want, and it returns real SVG markup ready to drop into a product or landing page.

Under the hood it combines two services. A Context.dev MCP connection resolves the brand facts first: name, description, colors, logos, homepage copy, and styleguide cues for a domain. Then a generate_svg_with_arrow tool calls the quiverai/arrow-1.1 image model through Vercel AI Gateway once per asset brief, validates that the response is safe SVG with a viewBox, rescales it to the requested dimensions, and normalizes icons to currentColor strokes so they theme automatically.

What makes it useful is pack coherence and honesty. A bundled brand-visual-assets skill enforces a six-step workflow with a scorecard: every asset must share palette, stroke language, and illustration metaphors, and anything scoring 8 or below gets regenerated with a tighter brief. If Context.dev or AI Gateway credentials fail, the agent stops and reports the error instead of fabricating brand facts or hand-writing replacement SVGs.
howItWorks: You send a request in chat, such as a feature launch pack for linear.app; if no website, product description, or brand profile is given, the agent asks for one before doing any generation work.

The agent calls the context-dev MCP connection (search_docs and execute against the hosted Context.dev server) to retrieve brand data, homepage markdown, and styleguide details, authenticating with your CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY via the x-context-dev-api-key header.

The brand-visual-assets skill scopes the pack, falling back to a default asset list if you did not name specific types, then locks a brand profile with primary and secondary hex colors, tone adjectives, and up to four reference images such as Context.dev logo or screenshot URLs.

For each asset it writes a self-contained brief and calls generate_svg_with_arrow once, which prompts quiverai/arrow-1.1 through Vercel AI Gateway, rejects output lacking a viewBox or containing scripts and raster content, fits the artwork to your requested dimensions, and adds title and desc elements for accessibility.
The agent scores every generated asset against the skill's quality-bar, consistency, and visual-taste references, then regenerates any asset scoring 8 or below on the scorecard with a tighter brief.

The final reply contains a brand brief with source URLs, an asset pack manifest with filenames and purposes, one fenced svg block per asset, usage notes for theming and placement, and an assumptions section when choices were inferred. Two bundled evals verify the ask-first and no-fabrication behaviors.

useCases.title: Feature launch pack from a domain
useCases.body: Point the agent at your marketing site and request a hero illustration, feature icons, a new-feature badge, and an onboarding visual. Context.dev extracts your palette and logos so every asset lands on brand without manual specs.

useCases.title: Empty states for a pre-launch product
useCases.body: No public website yet? Provide a product description, a primary hex color, and tone adjectives, and the agent generates empty-state and modal illustrations directly from that explicit brand profile, listing its assumptions alongside the SVGs.

useCases.title: Themeable icon sets for a design system
useCases.body: Request feature, navigation, or status icons and get SVGs normalized to currentColor strokes with fill none, a 1.8 stroke width, and rounded caps, so the icons inherit text color and work in light and dark themes.

useCases.title: Changelog and release visuals on demand
useCases.body: Generate consistent changelog art or dashboard graphics for each release. Because the skill enforces shared palette and stroke language across the pack, week-over-week visuals stay coherent instead of drifting in style.

requirements.name: CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY
requirements.body: Context.dev API key used by the MCP connection for brand, webpage, and styleguide extraction; sent only from the eve runtime as the x-context-dev-api-key header. Create one in your Context.dev account. CONTEXT_API_KEY is accepted as a fallback name.

requirements.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
requirements.body: Vercel AI Gateway key (vck_ prefix) that lets generate_svg_with_arrow call the quiverai/arrow-1.1 image model. Create it in your Vercel AI Gateway project and make sure that model is enabled there.

requirements.name: VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN
requirements.body: Alternative AI Gateway credential. On Vercel deployments it is provided automatically; locally you can pull one with the Vercel CLI. Set either this or AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, not necessarily both.

requirements.name: eve, ai, zod
requirements.body: Runtime dependencies installed with the registry item: the eve framework (^0.47.5), the ai SDK (^7.0.38) for generateImage, and zod 4.4.3 for tool input validation. Node.js 24 or newer is required.

faqs.question: How do I install and run this agent?
faqs.answer: Run npx shadcn@latest add @evex/brand-visual-asset-generator in your eve app, copy .env.example into your environment with the Context.dev and AI Gateway credentials filled in, then start the app with pnpm dev and ask for a visual pack in chat.

faqs.question: Which models does it use?
faqs.answer: The root orchestrator runs on deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, and SVG generation uses quiverai/arrow-1.1 called through Vercel AI Gateway's image-generation endpoint. Your deployment needs access to both providers; the agent never asks a language model to draw the SVGs itself.

faqs.question: Can I customize the assets it produces?
faqs.answer: Yes. Name the exact asset types, dimensions, colors, and tone in your request, or let the skill fall back to its default pack. You can also pass up to four reference images per asset for style, palette, composition, or typography direction, stating what to preserve and what to change.

faqs.question: Does it work without a company website?
faqs.answer: Yes. Instead of a domain, give a product description or an explicit brand profile such as a primary hex color, audience, and tone adjectives. The agent skips Context.dev extraction only when you supply the brand facts, and it records inferred choices in an assumptions section.

faqs.question: What are the known limits and failure modes?
faqs.answer: Arrow 1.1 accepts at most four reference images and about 6000 output tokens per asset. Context.dev can return 408 or 429 on cold starts and rate limits, so retry or reduce concurrency. On missing credentials or model errors the agent stops and reports the failure rather than fabricating output.

components.name: branded-seo-page-builder
components.title: Branded SEO Page Builder
components.description: Generate an on-brand, SEO-optimized HTML page from a domain using Context.dev brand, content, and styleguide data.

overview: Branded SEO Page Builder is an eve agent that turns a bare domain into one complete, SEO-optimized HTML page. You interact with it in chat: ask for a page from a domain such as linear.app, or point it at a specific source URL and a target topic, and it returns a full static document with metadata, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, semantic sections, and JSON-LD structured data.

What makes it useful is grounding. The agent connects to Context.dev's hosted MCP server at context-dev.stlmcp.com to resolve real brand data for the domain: company name, description, colors, logos, industry labels, homepage content as markdown, and optional styleguide signals like typography and spacing. Every user-facing claim in the generated page comes from that data or your explicit request, never invented statistics, testimonials, or pricing.

Two vendored skills shape the output. The seo-audit skill enforces on-page fundamentals such as one h1, canonical tags, descriptive alt text, and intent-matched schema types, while the ai-seo skill structures copy into extractable answer blocks and FAQ sections so answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews can cite the page, not only rank it.
howItWorks: You ask for a page in chat, for example 'Create an SEO-optimized landing page for linear.app'; if no domain is given, the agent stops and asks for one before doing any generation work.

It loads the bundled seo-audit skill to plan page structure, metadata, headings, canonical tags, image alt text, and schema, then loads the ai-seo skill before writing body copy so sections stay extractable and answer-oriented.

Through the context-dev MCP connection it discovers Context.dev tools via connection_search, consults search_docs for exact SDK method names, and calls execute to fetch brand data, page markdown, and styleguide details for the domain.

It infers the most useful page intent from the request and the retrieved data, choosing between homepage, landing, feature, comparison, local, or product page, and only asks a follow-up when the data cannot support a sensible choice.

It generates one complete HTML document with inline CSS reflecting the brand's colors and typography, a single h1, Open Graph and Twitter card tags, an FAQ section when it fits, and JSON-LD using Organization, WebPage, FAQPage, Product, or Service.

It returns the document in a single fenced html block followed by SEO notes covering search intent, primary keyword, secondary topics, schema types, and Context.dev source URLs, plus an assumptions list whenever copy relied on inference; two bundled evals verify the missing-domain guard and this page-structure contract.

useCases.title: Landing page from a domain in minutes
useCases.body: Give the agent a prospect's or your own domain and get a launch-ready static landing page whose copy, colors, and typography match the live brand, complete with metadata and structured data for immediate deployment.

useCases.title: Programmatic SEO page drafts
useCases.body: Generate grounded first drafts for feature, comparison, or product pages by pointing the agent at a specific source URL and target keyword, such as building a product page targeting AI support automation.

useCases.title: AI answer engine visibility
useCases.body: Produce pages structured for citation by ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews, with extractable answer blocks, FAQ sections, and FAQPage schema, while staying people-first to avoid scaled content abuse penalties.

useCases.title: On-brand pages for agency clients
useCases.body: Agencies can prototype an SEO page for any client domain without collecting brand assets manually; Context.dev supplies logos, colors, industry labels, and homepage copy so the draft looks like the client made it.

requirements.name: CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY
requirements.body: Context.dev API key used to authenticate the hosted MCP server at context-dev.stlmcp.com via the x-context-dev-api-key header. Create one in your Context.dev account; keys look like ctxt_secret_. The agent refuses to run brand lookups without it.

requirements.body: Optional fallback variable read when CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY is unset, for projects that already use this name. CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY is the documented standard; set only one of the two.

requirements.body: The eve framework runtime that hosts the agent, its MCP client connection, skills, and evals. Installed as the registry item's dependency; the agent package requires Node 24 or newer.

requirements.name: ai@^7.0.38
requirements.body: The Vercel AI SDK runtime required by eve ^0.47.5. It is installed automatically with this registry item; no separate manual setup is required.

faqs.question: How do I install and run it?
faqs.answer: Run npx shadcn@latest add @evex/branded-seo-page-builder in your eve app, copy .env.example and set CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY, then start with pnpm dev and ask the agent in chat for a page from any domain.

faqs.question: Which model does the agent use?
faqs.answer: It is configured with zai/glm-5.2-fast in agent/agent.ts. You can swap the model by editing the defineAgent call; the instructions, skills, and Context.dev connection work independently of the model choice.

faqs.question: What output do I actually get?
faqs.answer: One complete HTML document in a single fenced html block with inline CSS and no JavaScript unless requested, followed by SEO notes listing search intent, primary keyword, secondary topics, schema types, and Context.dev source URLs, plus assumptions when copy was inferred.

faqs.question: What happens if Context.dev has little data for a domain, or the API fails?
faqs.answer: The agent will not fabricate brand facts. On a missing or invalid key, a 401, or a 429 rate limit it stops and reports the failure; with thin brand data it asks for more source copy or a specific page URL instead of inventing claims.

faqs.question: Can I customize the visual style or page type?
faqs.answer: Yes. By default the agent applies Context.dev styleguide data for colors, typography, spacing, and shadows. You can pass a specific source page URL, request a particular intent like a comparison or product page, or ask it to skip styleguide data entirely.

components.name: code-reviewer
components.title: Code Reviewer
components.description: Eve agent for GitHub PR review. Mention it on a PR for inline comments on bugs, not style.

overview: Code Reviewer is an eve agent that reviews GitHub pull requests when someone mentions @code-reviewer in a PR comment or a review thread. It runs behind a native GitHub App channel: GitHub delivers the comment webhook to your deployed eve app at /eve/v1/github, and the agent replies by publishing a real GitHub review with inline comments anchored to the diff.

The agent reviews changed behavior, not style. Its instructions direct it at concrete bugs, regressions, security risks, rollout risk, and materially missing tests, and explicitly forbid naming nits and speculative rewrites. It labels each finding blocking, warning, or nit, caps each review at 10 inline comments, and attaches GitHub suggestion blocks for small local fixes the author applies manually.

It is read-only toward your repository: the channel checks the code out into the eve sandbox for inspection, but the agent never pushes commits, opens branches, or edits the pull request. Built-in Upstash-backed rate limiting keeps public deployments safe, with stricter defaults for public repositories than private ones.
howItWorks: A user comments @code-reviewer (the mention must match GITHUB_APP_SLUG) on a pull request timeline or in a Files changed review thread, and GitHub sends the webhook to the eve app.

The channel verifies the mention targets a pull request conversation, then checks Upstash rate limits: per-PR cooldown, per-user-per-PR cooldown, and daily repository quotas; if blocked, it posts at most one cooldown reply per 15 minutes instead of running the model.
When allowed, the channel injects PR metadata and diff context (excluding lockfiles and build output like dist, .next, and coverage) and checks the repository out into the eve sandbox.

The agent, running on the zai/glm-5.2 model, inspects only the context needed to validate findings using read_file, grep, glob, and targeted bash, loading the bundled review-calibration skill when severity is ambiguous.
It calls the submit_pr_review tool exactly once with a summary and up to 10 severity-labeled inline comments, each validated by a Zod schema (path, line, side, optional suggestion block).

The channel claims the publication in Redis to prevent duplicates, then posts a batch GitHub review; if batch creation fails, it falls back to individual inline comments plus a timeline summary, and reviews with no findings become a short timeline comment.

useCases.title: On-demand review for team pull requests
useCases.body: Install the GitHub App on your team repositories and mention @code-reviewer when a PR is ready. You get a structured review with blocking, warning, and nit findings anchored to the exact diff lines, focused on bugs and regressions rather than style.

useCases.title: Safe reviews on public open-source repos
useCases.body: The Upstash-backed limiter defaults to 10 reviews per public repository per day, one review per PR every 15 minutes, and a per-user cooldown of 30 minutes, so drive-by mentions on a public repo cannot exhaust your model budget.

useCases.title: Quick-fix suggestions authors can apply in one click
useCases.body: For short, local, near-certain fixes the agent attaches a GitHub suggestion block to the inline comment. The PR author applies it from the GitHub UI; the agent itself never commits or modifies the branch.

useCases.title: Second pass on risky surfaces before merge
useCases.body: The instructions prioritize auth, permissions, user data, schemas, cache invalidation, concurrency, and billing code paths. Mention the agent on high-risk PRs to get a focused pass on those surfaces plus residual-risk notes in the review summary.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_ID
requirements.body: The App ID of the GitHub App you create under GitHub Settings, Developer settings, GitHub Apps. The app needs Metadata read, Contents read, Pull requests read/write, and Issues read/write permissions.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
requirements.body: The PEM private key generated from the GitHub App settings page. When stored as a single-line variable, replace literal newlines with \n; eve normalizes that form at runtime.

requirements.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
requirements.body: A long random value set both in the GitHub App webhook configuration and in your deployment. A mismatch produces HTTP 401 responses at /eve/v1/github.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_SLUG
requirements.body: The mention users type on GitHub, defaulting to code-reviewer. It must match your GitHub App name so @code-reviewer mentions trigger the agent.

requirements.name: KV_REST_API_URL
requirements.body: Upstash Redis REST endpoint used by @upstash/ratelimit for cooldowns, daily quotas, and duplicate-publication claims. Provision it via Upstash or the Vercel Redis Marketplace integration.

requirements.name: KV_REST_API_TOKEN
requirements.body: The matching Upstash REST token. Use a read-write token, not the read-only one, because the agent writes cooldown and review publication keys.

requirements.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
requirements.body: A model credential for the deployment, either a Vercel AI Gateway API key or AI Gateway OIDC, so the agent can call the zai/glm-5.2 model.

faqs.question: How do I install and trigger it?
faqs.answer: Run npx shadcn@latest add @evex/code-reviewer inside an eve app, deploy it over HTTPS, create a GitHub App pointing its webhook at /eve/v1/github, subscribe to Issue comments and Pull request review comments, install it on your repositories, then comment @code-reviewer review this on any pull request.

faqs.question: Can it modify my pull request?
faqs.answer: No. The agent only publishes review comments and optional suggestion blocks. It may test small patches inside the eve sandbox to validate a suggestion, but it never pushes commits, opens branches, or edits the PR; authors apply suggestions manually.

faqs.question: Which model does it use and can I change it?
faqs.answer: The agent is pinned to zai/glm-5.2 in agent/agent.ts. Since the file is installed into your app, you can edit defineAgent to point at any model available through your AI Gateway credential.

faqs.question: How do the rate limits work and can I tune them?
faqs.answer: Defaults are one review per PR every 15 minutes, one per user per PR every 30 minutes, 25 daily reviews per private repository, and 10 per public repository. Every limit is tunable via CODE_REVIEWER_* environment variables, and CODE_REVIEWER_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false disables limiting for local development.

faqs.question: What happens if Upstash is unreachable?
faqs.answer: The failure mode defaults to public_closed: reviews on public repositories are blocked while private repositories continue working. You can change CODE_REVIEWER_RATE_LIMIT_FAILURE_MODE to closed or open depending on how conservative you want the deployment to be.

components.name: competitor-intel-monitor
components.title: Competitor Intel Monitor
components.description: Scheduled competitor URL monitor that diffs pages and delivers scored Slack or email digests.

overview: Competitor Intel Monitor is a scheduled eve agent that re-reads a list of competitor pages you already chose. On each cron tick it checks robots.txt, pulls the HTML that is allowed, and compares normalized text to the last snapshot in a JSON file or Upstash Redis. You configure the list and thresholds once, then leave it running.

You interact with it through environment variables and your inbox or Slack. Set COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS or a JSON or text file, pick Slack, Resend, or both, and trigger watch-competitor-pages. The agent previews every digest and only sends when confirmSend is true and a date-derived idempotency key is present.

It is useful when you want a quiet baseline plus alerts that ignore tiny edits. First-seen URLs are stored without a ping. Later diffs report a score from changed character weight, and only rows that clear both gates go out. Robots disallows and missing config stop that path instead of inventing a page.
howItWorks: On the watch-competitor-pages schedule (cron from COMPETITOR_INTEL_CRON, default 08:00 UTC), the agent loads the competitor-intel-watch skill and, before any email, the email-best-practices skill.
It calls load_watch_config to read the https URL list, alert gates, store kind, and whether Slack or email is configured, and stops if COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS or delivery settings are missing.

For each listed URL it calls fetch_competitor_page, which loads that origin's robots.txt with EveCompetitorIntelMonitor/1.0 and skips the page when robots disallows the path or the robots file cannot be reached.

Each successful fetch goes to diff_page_snapshot, which compares normalized text to the stored snapshot, writes the new snapshot, and returns score, changedChars, and clearsThreshold. First-seen URLs are baselines with score 0.

If any row clears both COMPETITOR_INTEL_ALERT_MIN_SCORE and COMPETITOR_INTEL_ALERT_MIN_CHANGED_CHARS, the agent calls preview_digest, then send_digest with confirmSend true and an idempotency key such as competitor-intel-monitor-YYYY-MM-DD.
Seven evals cover the schedule path, robots skips, below-threshold silence, digest preview, send confirmation, missing config, and a failed send that must not be reported as delivered.

useCases.title: Pricing page drift
useCases.body: Point the watch list at two competitor pricing URLs. After the first baseline run, a later seat-price rewrite that clears the score and character gates lands in Slack or email with the excerpt from diff_page_snapshot.

useCases.title: Changelog without the noise
useCases.body: Watch a public changelog. A one-word typo stays under COMPETITOR_INTEL_ALERT_MIN_CHANGED_CHARS and is stored only. A new version notes section that clears both gates is the row that gets previewed.

useCases.title: Robots-respecting research crawl
useCases.body: A competitor blocks /compare in robots.txt. fetch_competitor_page returns blockedByRobots for that path, the agent skips it, and send_digest is never called for an invented compare table.

useCases.title: Team alias on a weekday cron
useCases.body: Set COMPETITOR_INTEL_CRON to weekday mornings and COMPETITOR_INTEL_DIGEST_TO to a team alias. Operators get one Resend HTML mail with the URLs that cleared the gates, not a ping for every tiny HTML shuffle.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS
requirements.body: Comma-separated https URLs to watch. Required unless COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS_FILE lists at least one https URL. Non-https values are dropped.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS_FILE
requirements.body: Optional JSON object with urls and alert, or a text file with one URL per line. Those URLs are unioned with COMPETITOR_INTEL_URLS.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_CRON
requirements.body: 5-field cron for watch-competitor-pages. Defaults to 0 8 * * * (08:00 UTC on Vercel).

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_ALERT_MIN_SCORE
requirements.body: Minimum score from 0 to 100. Score is round(100 * changedChars / max(beforeLength, afterLength, 1)). Defaults to 25.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_ALERT_MIN_CHANGED_CHARS
requirements.body: Minimum added-plus-removed character weight before a change can clear the gate. Defaults to 40.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_STORE_PATH
requirements.body: JSON snapshot file path. Defaults to .data/competitor-intel-store.json. Use a durable volume if the app filesystem is ephemeral.

requirements.name: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL
requirements.body: Optional Upstash Redis REST URL. When set with UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN, snapshots are stored in Redis instead of the file.

requirements.name: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN
requirements.body: Optional Upstash Redis REST token used with UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_USER_AGENT
requirements.body: User-Agent for page and robots.txt fetches. Defaults to EveCompetitorIntelMonitor/1.0.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_SLACK_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Optional Vercel Connect Slack connector UID for the Eve Slack channel. Leave empty to skip Slack. At least one of Slack Connect or a complete email trio is required to send.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
requirements.body: Optional Slack channel id for the digest. Leave empty to skip Slack. Both this and COMPETITOR_INTEL_SLACK_CONNECT_UID must be set to post.

requirements.name: @vercel/connect
requirements.body: Runtime dependency that supplies Slack credentials through connectSlackCredentials. send_digest posts with Eve callSlackApi after approval, not an incoming webhook.

requirements.name: RESEND_API_KEY
requirements.body: Resend API key used by send_digest when email recipients are configured. The idempotency key is forwarded to Resend.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_DIGEST_FROM
requirements.body: Verified Resend sender for the HTML digest. Recipients and sender cannot be overridden through tool input.

requirements.name: COMPETITOR_INTEL_DIGEST_TO
requirements.body: Comma-separated recipient addresses. Optional COMPETITOR_INTEL_DIGEST_SUBJECT defaults to Competitor intel digest.

faqs.question: How do I install and run a watch?
faqs.answer: Install with npx shadcn@latest add @evex/competitor-intel-monitor, copy .env.example, set at least one https URL plus Slack or Resend, then POST to /eve/v1/dev/schedules/watch-competitor-pages while iterating.

faqs.question: Will the first run email or Slack me?
faqs.answer: No. diff_page_snapshot stores a first-seen URL as a baseline with score 0 and clearsThreshold false. Only a later run whose score and changedChars both clear the gates can call preview_digest and send_digest.

faqs.question: What if robots.txt blocks a URL?
faqs.answer: fetch_competitor_page returns blockedByRobots and skips the HTTP body. The agent records the skip, does not invent text, and does not send a digest for that URL.

faqs.question: How is the score calculated?
faqs.answer: changedChars is the character weight of words added or removed after HTML is stripped. score is round(100 * changedChars / max(beforeLength, afterLength, 1)), capped at 100. Both that score and minChangedChars must pass.

faqs.question: Can a replayed run send twice?
faqs.answer: send_digest refuses unless confirmSend is true, and it requires a stable idempotency key. Successful sends are cached on that key and the same key is sent to Resend, so a replayed eve step does not duplicate email.

components.name: crm-hygiene-agent
components.title: CRM Hygiene Agent
components.description: Scheduled CRM hygiene via Connect that proposes dedupe, normalize, and enrich batches for human approval before any write.

overview: CRM Hygiene Agent is an eve agent that connects to one HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive account you already own. On each cron tick it reads contacts through Vercel Connect, drafts a dedupe, normalize, and enrich batch, and waits for you to approve before any CRM write.

You interact with it through environment variables and Slack or email. Set a Connect UID for the CRM you use, pick Slack Connect, Resend, or both, and trigger crm-hygiene-scan. The agent previews every digest and only delivers when confirmSend is true. CRM writes stay behind apply_hygiene_writes.

It is useful when you want scheduled cleanup without silent merges. Duplicate emails become a reviewable dedupe row. Name and phone formatting become normalize rows. Empty company or phone fields become enrich rows that copy from a sibling on the same domain. The append-only audit log records proposed, delivered, approved, written, and refused.
howItWorks: On the crm-hygiene-scan schedule (cron from CRM_HYGIENE_CRON, default 08:00 UTC), the agent loads the crm-hygiene skill.
It calls load_crm_config and stops when a HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive Connect UID is missing, or when neither Slack nor email delivery is configured.
scan_crm_records mints a Vercel Connect token and lists contacts. That tool is read-only and never merges or patches a record.
propose_hygiene_batch drafts dedupe, normalize, and enrich work, writes the batch into the append-only audit log, and returns written false.

If the batch has proposals, the agent calls preview_hygiene_digest, then deliver_hygiene_digest with confirmSend true. That tool pauses for Eve approval before the Slack Connect channel or Resend. The cron path does not call apply_hygiene_writes.
Four evals cover the schedule path, digest preview, writes that require approval, and a run that must not apply without confirmWrite.

useCases.title: Duplicate emails waiting for a human
useCases.body: Two HubSpot contacts share ava@example.com. propose_hygiene_batch adds a dedupe row. Slack gets the draft batch. apply_hygiene_writes runs only after you approve with confirmWrite true.

useCases.title: Name and phone cleanup
useCases.body: A Salesforce contact has firstName ava and a ten-digit phone. The normalize proposal title-cases the name and prefixes plus on the phone. Nothing is patched until apply_hygiene_writes is approved.

useCases.title: Fill empty company from a sibling
useCases.body: A Pipedrive person on example.com has no company. Another person on that domain lists Acme. The enrich row copies Acme into the empty field and never overwrites a filled company.

useCases.title: Monday cron, Slack review
useCases.body: Set CRM_HYGIENE_CRON to weekday mornings and Slack Connect. Operators get one draft batch in the Eve Slack channel. The cron path stops after deliver_hygiene_digest. Writes wait for chat plus approval.

requirements.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
requirements.body: A model credential for the deployment, either a Vercel AI Gateway API key or AI Gateway OIDC, so the agent can call zai/glm-5.2.

requirements.name: CRM_PROVIDER
requirements.body: Optional force of hubspot, salesforce, or pipedrive. When empty, the first complete Connect UID wins.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_CRON
requirements.body: 5-field cron for crm-hygiene-scan. Defaults to 0 8 * * * (08:00 UTC on Vercel).

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_MAX_RECORDS
requirements.body: Maximum contacts to read per scan. Defaults to 100.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_AUDIT_PATH
requirements.body: Append-only JSONL audit log. Defaults to .data/crm-hygiene-audit.jsonl. Stores identifiers, proposal kinds, and changed field names only. Use a durable volume if the app filesystem is ephemeral.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS
requirements.body: Days to keep audit rows. Defaults to 90. propose_hygiene_batch purges older rows.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_DEFAULT_PHONE_COUNTRY_CODE
requirements.body: Optional country calling code, digits only, used before adding + to a national phone. Leave empty to leave non-E.164 numbers unchanged.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_SLACK_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Optional Vercel Connect Slack connector UID for the Eve Slack channel. Leave empty to skip Slack delivery.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
requirements.body: Optional Slack channel id for the draft batch. Leave empty to skip Slack delivery.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_HUBSPOT_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Vercel Connect HubSpot connector UID from vercel connect create hubspot. Mints crm.objects.contacts.read, crm.objects.contacts.write, and crm.objects.companies.read. Writes still require apply_hygiene_writes after Eve approval.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_SALESFORCE_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Vercel Connect Salesforce connector UID from vercel connect create salesforce. Mints api and refresh_token.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_SALESFORCE_INSTANCE_URL
requirements.body: HTTPS Salesforce instance URL required when the provider is salesforce.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_PIPEDRIVE_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Vercel Connect Pipedrive connector UID from vercel connect create pipedrive. Mints contacts:read and contacts:full.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_PIPEDRIVE_COMPANY_DOMAIN
requirements.body: Optional Pipedrive company domain. The runtime talks to api.pipedrive.com with the Connect token.

requirements.name: RESEND_API_KEY
requirements.body: Resend API key used by deliver_hygiene_digest when email recipients are configured. The idempotency key is forwarded to Resend.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_DIGEST_FROM
requirements.body: Verified Resend sender for the HTML digest. Recipients and sender cannot be overridden through tool input.

requirements.name: CRM_HYGIENE_DIGEST_TO
requirements.body: Comma-separated recipient addresses. Optional CRM_HYGIENE_DIGEST_SUBJECT defaults to CRM hygiene batch.

faqs.question: How do I install and run a scan?
faqs.answer: Install with npx shadcn@latest add @evex/crm-hygiene-agent, copy .env.example, set one CRM Connect UID plus Slack or Resend, then POST to /eve/v1/dev/schedules/crm-hygiene-scan while iterating.

faqs.question: Does the cron path write to the CRM?
faqs.answer: No. crm-hygiene-scan reads, proposes, and may deliver a digest after approval. apply_hygiene_writes is the only write path and is not called on cron. confirmWrite must be true after a later Eve approval.

faqs.question: Is Slack required?
faqs.answer: No. CRM_HYGIENE_SLACK_CONNECT_UID and CRM_HYGIENE_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID are optional. When both are set, deliver_hygiene_digest posts the draft batch through the Eve Slack channel. That ping is not a CRM write.

faqs.question: How do I approve a cleanup batch?
faqs.answer: Review the Slack or email digest, then call apply_hygiene_writes with the proposed batch and confirmWrite true. The tool always pauses for Eve approval. Without that grant the CRM client refuses POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE.

faqs.question: What if two contacts share an email?
faqs.answer: propose_hygiene_batch adds a dedupe row that keeps the fuller record as primary. The merge stays staged until you approve apply_hygiene_writes. There is no auto-merge and no silent overwrite.

components.name: docs-knowledge-assistant
components.title: Docs Knowledge Assistant
components.description: Answers from your repo docs and cites the file.

overview: Docs Knowledge Assistant is an eve agent that answers questions from the installing repository's documentation files. It searches README, docs/, CONTRIBUTING*, and AGENTS.md, then replies with file-path citations so readers can verify the source.

You interact with it through Eve chat sessions or by mentioning it on a GitHub issue comment. It ignores pull request conversations, never publishes GitHub PR reviews, and never applies taxonomy labels or triage other issues.

When the documentation clearly lacks an answer, it says so. On GitHub issue-comment turns it can optionally open a documentation-gap issue with open_docs_issue so maintainers can track missing docs without turning the agent into a second issue bot.
howItWorks: A user asks a documentation question in Eve chat, or mentions @docs-knowledge-assistant on a GitHub issue comment matching GITHUB_APP_SLUG.
The GitHub channel rejects pull request conversations and review threads, then injects issue context for the zai/glm-5.2 model.
The agent loads the docs-qa skill when needed, then calls search_docs and read_doc, which refuse non-documentation paths and discover README.* / CONTRIBUTING.* variants at the repo root.
It answers from those files only and cites each path it relied on. write_file is disabled so the agent cannot rewrite the repository as an answer.

If the docs do not cover the question, it says so. On GitHub issue-comment turns only, a clear gap may call open_docs_issue once; Eve chat receives readyToOpen false because no GitHub publisher runs there. The channel creates the issue through the GitHub Issues API without applying taxonomy labels.
Evals cover answering with a README citation, saying not-in-docs, and refusing PR review or labeling requests.

useCases.title: Install and setup questions from README
useCases.body: New contributors ask how to install or configure the project in Eve chat. The agent reads README.md or docs/install.md and answers with the cited path instead of guessing from source.

useCases.title: Contributor workflow questions on GitHub issues
useCases.body: Mention the bot on an issue asking about contribution steps. It answers from CONTRIBUTING* or AGENTS.md and posts the cited reply on the issue timeline.

useCases.title: Honest gaps when docs are silent
useCases.body: When someone asks about on-call policy or an undocumented API, the agent says the docs do not cover it rather than inventing steps from application source.

useCases.title: Track missing documentation
useCases.body: When a recurring question on a GitHub issue has no docs home, open_docs_issue creates a focused documentation issue so maintainers can fill the gap without labeling or triaging other work.

requirements.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
requirements.body: A model credential for the deployment, either a Vercel AI Gateway API key or AI Gateway OIDC, so the agent can call the zai/glm-5.2 model.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_ID
requirements.body: Optional. The App ID of the GitHub App used for issue-comment Q&A. Needs Metadata read, Contents read, and Issues read/write. Do not grant Pull requests write.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
requirements.body: Optional. The PEM private key for the GitHub App. When stored as a single-line variable, replace literal newlines with \n.

requirements.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
requirements.body: Optional. Shared secret for verifying GitHub webhooks at /eve/v1/github. A mismatch produces HTTP 401.

requirements.name: GITHUB_APP_SLUG
requirements.body: Optional. The mention users type on GitHub, defaulting to docs-knowledge-assistant. It must match your GitHub App name.

faqs.question: How do I install and ask a question?
faqs.answer: Run npx shadcn@latest add @evex/docs-knowledge-assistant inside an eve app, set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, then ask documentation questions in Eve chat. For GitHub issue replies, deploy over HTTPS, create a GitHub App pointing at /eve/v1/github, and mention the bot on an issue.

faqs.question: Does it review pull requests or label issues?
faqs.answer: No. The channel ignores pull request conversations, there is no PR review publication path, and it never applies taxonomy labels. Use @evex/code-reviewer for PR reviews and @evex/github-issue-maintainer for issue triage.

faqs.question: Which files can it read?
faqs.answer: Only README*, docs/**, CONTRIBUTING*, and AGENTS.md. search_docs and read_doc refuse application source, tests, and config paths.

faqs.question: What happens when the docs do not answer?
faqs.answer: The agent says the documentation does not cover the question. On GitHub issue-comment turns, when the gap is clear, it can call open_docs_issue to create a documentation issue without labeling other issues. Eve chat refuses that tool.

faqs.question: Is GitHub required?
faqs.answer: No. Chat works with only AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. GitHub App credentials are needed only for issue-comment Q&A and optional docs-gap issue creation.

components.name: email-triage-assistant
components.title: Email Triage Assistant
components.description: Inbox triage that classifies threads and writes draft replies without sending.

overview: Email Triage Assistant is an eve agent that connects to one mailbox you already own. On each cron tick or signed inbox push it lists threads, reads the ones that need a human, and writes replies into the provider Drafts folder. You review those drafts in Gmail, Outlook, or IMAP and hit send yourself.

You interact with it through the inbox-triage schedule, the /inbox/push channel, or an on-demand Eve chat that still reads the mailbox. Set EMAIL_TRIAGE_GOOGLE_CONNECT_UID, EMAIL_TRIAGE_MICROSOFT_CONNECT_UID, or IMAP, plus optional Slack Connect. The agent applies TRIAGE_BUCKETS labels and matches Sent-folder tone before it calls create_draft_reply.

It is useful when you want autonomous sorting without an auto-send. Code refuses SMTP ports and send URLs. create_draft_reply always returns sent false. Newsletter and FYI threads get a bucket and no draft unless a real question is waiting in the thread.
howItWorks: On the inbox-triage schedule (cron from EMAIL_TRIAGE_CRON, default every two hours UTC) or a signed POST to /inbox/push, the agent loads the inbox-triage skill.
It calls load_inbox_config and stops when Gmail, Microsoft Graph, or IMAP credentials are missing. Push runs also call ingest_push_event.
list_inbox_threads and read_thread pull live mailbox data. sample_sent_style reads the Sent folder and returns a greeting, sign-off, and sentence-length brief.
apply_triage_bucket writes a Gmail triage/ label, an Outlook category, or an IMAP Triage/ folder for one configured TRIAGE_BUCKETS slug.
create_draft_reply writes Gmail drafts.create, Graph createReply, or IMAP APPEND to Drafts and always returns sent false. Optional notify_slack_drafts_ready posts a drafts-ready queue note.
Three evals cover never-send, triage buckets, and the schedule or push path so a paste-to-text skill shape cannot replace the mailbox loop.

useCases.title: Refund thread that stays in Drafts
useCases.body: A customer asks about an annual-plan refund. The agent reads the thread, applies needs-reply, writes a Sent-matched draft, and leaves it in Drafts for you to send.

useCases.title: Newsletter bucket, no draft
useCases.body: A weekly changelog lands in the IMAP inbox. apply_triage_bucket files it under newsletter. create_draft_reply is skipped because there is no question waiting in the thread.

useCases.title: Graph push during the day
useCases.body: Outlook posts a change notification to /inbox/push with EMAIL_PUSH_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The channel starts a mailbox run that drafts a reply without calling sendMail.

useCases.title: Slack queue when drafts pile up
useCases.body: After a cron run writes three Drafts, notify_slack_drafts_ready posts to the Eve Slack Connect channel. The note says drafts are ready. Nothing is emailed.

requirements.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
requirements.body: A model credential for the deployment, either a Vercel AI Gateway API key or AI Gateway OIDC, so the agent can call zai/glm-5.2.

requirements.name: EMAIL_PROVIDER
requirements.body: Optional force of gmail, outlook, or imap. When empty, the first complete credential set wins.

requirements.name: EMAIL_TRIAGE_CRON
requirements.body: 5-field cron for inbox-triage. Defaults to 0 */2 * * * (every two hours UTC on Vercel).

requirements.name: TRIAGE_BUCKETS
requirements.body: Comma-separated slugs. Defaults to needs-reply, fyi, waiting, urgent, newsletter, no-reply.

requirements.name: EMAIL_MAX_THREADS
requirements.body: Maximum inbox threads to list per run. Defaults to 20.

requirements.name: EMAIL_SENT_SAMPLE_SIZE
requirements.body: How many Sent-folder messages to sample for tone. Defaults to 8.

requirements.name: EMAIL_PUSH_WEBHOOK_SECRET
requirements.body: Shared secret for POST /inbox/push. Graph validationToken echoes do not require it.

requirements.name: EMAIL_TRIAGE_SLACK_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Optional Vercel Connect Slack connector UID for the Eve Slack channel. Leave empty to skip Slack notify.

requirements.name: EMAIL_TRIAGE_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
requirements.body: Optional Slack channel id for the drafts-ready note. Leave empty to skip Slack notify.

requirements.name: EMAIL_TRIAGE_GOOGLE_CONNECT_UID
requirements.body: Vercel Connect Google connector UID from vercel connect create google. Mints gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, and gmail.modify tokens. The agent never calls messages.send or drafts.send.

requirements.name: GMAIL_USER
requirements.body: Optional From address written onto Gmail drafts.

requirements.name: EMAIL_TRIAGE_MICROSOFT_CONNECT_UID
